# 🍎 macOS Systems & Darwin Engineering Track

Welcome to the **macOS Systems & Darwin Engineering Track** materialized by **Trak**.

This workspace is an in-depth curriculum covering Darwin kernel architecture (XNU), APFS filesystem mechanics, launchd service management, Homebrew packaging, Apple Silicon universal binaries, and macOS security (SIP, Gatekeeper, TCC).

## 📚 Syllabus & Module Map

| Module | Title | Key Topics & Internals |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-darwin-architecture` | Darwin & XNU Kernel | XNU architecture (Mach microkernel + BSD), `sw_vers`, System Integrity Protection (SIP) |
| `01-homebrew-and-package-management` | Homebrew & Brew Services | `/opt/homebrew` (ARM64) vs `/usr/local` (Intel), `brew cask`, `brew services` |
| `02-zsh-and-macos-shell-environment` | Zsh & Terminal Config | `.zshrc`, `.zprofile`, environment variables, macOS default shell |
| `03-file-system-apfs-and-extended-attributes` | APFS & Extended Attributes | Copy-on-write clones, snapshots, extended attributes (`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine`) |
| `04-launchd-services-and-daemons` | `launchd` & Plist Daemons | LaunchDaemons vs LaunchAgents, plist XML format, `launchctl bootstrap/bootout` |
| `05-process-management-and-activity-monitor` | Processes & Thermal States | `ps`, `top`, thermal state monitoring (`pmset -g therm`), memory pressure |
| `06-macos-system-preferences-and-defaults` | `defaults` & Plist Editing | `defaults write com.apple.finder`, `plutil -p`, system preference domains |
| `07-security-gatekeeper-sip-and-tcc` | Gatekeeper, SIP & TCC | Gatekeeper quarantine, `csrutil status`, TCC privacy permissions DB |
| `08-networking-scutil-and-networksetup` | macOS Networking & DNS | `networksetup`, `scutil --dns`, `dscacheutil -flushcache`, dynamic DNS |
| `09-applescript-and-jxa` | Automation & `osascript` | AppleScript (`osascript -e`), JavaScript for Automation (JXA), UI automation |
| `10-diskutil-and-storage-management` | `diskutil` & Disk Images | `diskutil apfs`, APFS containers, `hdiutil attach/detach` DMG images |
| `11-developer-toolchain-xcode-and-metal` | Xcode CLI & Toolchain | `xcode-select --install`, `xcrun`, LLVM clang on macOS, Metal shaders |
| `12-universal-binaries-and-rosetta` | Universal 2 & Rosetta 2 | Mach-O fat binaries (`lipo -info`), Rosetta 2 translation (`arch -x86_64`) |
| `13-keychain-and-credential-security` | Keychain Access (`security`) | Secure credential storage, `security find-generic-password`, certificates |
| `14-power-management-and-pmset` | Power Management & `pmset` | Sleep assertions, battery health, `caffeinate` CLI utility |
| `15-logging-unified-logging-system` | Unified Logging System | `log stream --predicate`, `log show`, subsystems & categories |
| `16-automator-and-shortcuts-cli` | Shortcuts CLI & Automator | `shortcuts run`, Quick Actions, headless workflow automation |
| `17-testing-and-diagnostics` | Diagnostics & Sysdiagnose | `sysdiagnose`, kernel crash logs, diagnostic reports in `/Library/Logs` |
| `18-interview-questions-and-drills` | Interview Mastery Drills | Top 10 macOS Systems & Enterprise MDM gotchas + Production Diagnostic Drill |

---

## 🛠️ How to Practice
Each module contains:
- `README.md` — Deep theoretical explanation and architecture notes.
- `example.sh` — Fully runnable concept demonstration.
- `exercise/starter.sh` — Hands-on problem with `TODO` markers.
- `exercise/solution.sh` — Complete reference solution.

children.content:
# 00 — Darwin & XNU Kernel Architecture

## 🎯 What is XNU?
XNU ("X is Not Unix") is the hybrid operating system kernel powering macOS, iOS, and watchOS:
- **Mach Microkernel**: Handles IPC, thread scheduling, virtual memory (`vm_map`), and CPU core dispatching.
- **BSD Subsystem**: Provides POSIX APIs, process models, networking stack (BSD sockets), and filesystem interfaces.

children.name: example.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "=== 00: macOS Darwin Architecture ==="
if command -v sw_vers &>/dev/null; then
  sw_vers
  echo "Darwin Kernel: $(uname -v)"
else
  echo "Simulated macOS Environment (sw_vers command not in PATH)"
fi

children.name: starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
ARCH=$(uname -m)
if [ "$ARCH" = "arm64" ]; then
  echo "✔ Apple Silicon Architecture (arm64)"
elif [ "$ARCH" = "x86_64" ]; then
  echo "✔ Intel Architecture (x86_64)"
else
  echo "Unknown architecture: $ARCH"
fi

# 01 — Homebrew Package Management

## 🎯 Architecture Locations
- **Apple Silicon (ARM64)**: `/opt/homebrew`
- **Intel (x86_64)**: `/usr/local`

children.name: example.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "=== 01: Homebrew Prefix Detection ==="
if command -v brew &>/dev/null; then
  echo "Brew Prefix: $(brew --prefix)"
  echo "Brew Version: $(brew --version | head -1)"
else
  echo "Homebrew not installed."
fi

children.name: starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
FORMULA="git"
if command -v brew &>/dev/null && brew list "$FORMULA" &>/dev/null; then
  echo "✔ $FORMULA is installed via Homebrew!"
else
  echo "Formula '$FORMULA' is not installed via brew."
fi

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 02 — Zsh & macOS Shell Configuration

## 🎯 Dotfiles Load Order
1. `/etc/zshenv` -> `~/.zshenv` (Loaded for ALL shells)
2. `/etc/zprofile` -> `~/.zprofile` (Loaded for login shells)
3. `/etc/zshrc` -> `~/.zshrc` (Loaded for interactive shells)

children.name: example.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "=== 02: Default Shell Environment ==="
echo "Current SHELL: $SHELL"
echo "ZSH Version: ${ZSH_VERSION:-N/A}"

children.name: starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ -f "$HOME/.zshrc" ]; then
  echo "✔ ~/.zshrc exists (Size: $(stat -f "%z bytes" "$HOME/.zshrc" 2>/dev/null || echo "N/A"))"
else
  echo "~/.zshrc does not exist."
fi

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 03 — APFS & Extended Attributes (`xattr`)

## 🎯 Quarantine Attribute
When downloading files from the internet, macOS attaches `com.apple.quarantine` extended attribute:
```bash
xattr -l app.zip
xattr -d com.apple.quarantine app.zip
```

children.name: example.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "=== 03: Extended Attributes ==="
touch /tmp/quarantine_demo.txt
if command -v xattr &>/dev/null; then
  xattr -w com.trak.demo "verified" /tmp/quarantine_demo.txt
  echo "Attached custom attribute: $(xattr -p com.trak.demo /tmp/quarantine_demo.txt)"
fi
rm -f /tmp/quarantine_demo.txt

children.name: starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "Command: sudo xattr -r -d com.apple.quarantine /Applications/MyApp.app"

children.name: README.md
children.content:
# 04 — `launchd` Daemons & Agents

## 🎯 LaunchAgents vs LaunchDaemons
- **LaunchAgents (`~/Library/LaunchAgents` / `/Library/LaunchAgents`)**: Run per-user in GUI user session.
- **LaunchDaemons (`/Library/LaunchDaemons`)**: Run as `root` in system background.

children.name: example.sh
starter.sh
solution.sh
children.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/dev.trak.agent.plist
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>dev.trak.agent</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>/usr/local/bin/trak</string>
        <string>daemon</string>
    </array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
</plist>
EOF
echo "✔ Generated LaunchAgent plist file."
rm -f /tmp/dev.trak.agent.plist

# 06 — Plist Preferences & `defaults` Command

## 🎯 The `defaults` CLI
Allows programmatic modification of macOS user settings:
```bash
defaults write com.apple.finder AppleShowAllFiles -bool true
killall Finder
```

  defaults read -g AppleInterfaceStyle 2>/dev/null && echo "Dark Mode Active" || echo "Light Mode Active"
fi

# 07 — Gatekeeper, SIP & TCC Privacy

## 🎯 Security Pillars
- **SIP (System Integrity Protection)**: Protects `/System`, `/usr`, `/bin` from modifications even by `root`.
- **TCC (Transparency, Consent & Control)**: Controls app access to Microphone, Camera, Full Disk Access.

fi

else
  echo "Gatekeeper status check command: spctl --status"

children.content:
# 18 — High-Yield macOS Systems Interview Drills

## 🧠 Top 10 Gotchas
1. **XNU Hybrid Kernel**: Mach microkernel handles low-level primitives; BSD provides POSIX layer.
2. **SIP File Locks**: Even root cannot write to `/System` or `/usr/bin` under SIP.
3. **APFS CoW Clones**: Copying a 10GB file on APFS takes 0ms and uses 0 additional bytes.
4. **Quarantine Flag**: Blocks downloaded binary execution until approved in Privacy settings.
5. **LaunchAgent vs LaunchDaemon**: Agents run in GUI user session; Daemons run as system background root.
6. **Compressed Memory**: macOS aggressively compresses RAM pages instead of writing to disk swap.
7. **Universal 2 Mach-O**: Contains multiple architecture slices (`lipo`).
8. **TCC Privacy Database**: Stored in SQLite database protected by SIP.
9. **Rosetta 2 JIT Translation**: Ahead-of-Time translates x86_64 instructions on first launch.
10. **Keychain Access ACLs**: Access control lists govern which apps can read specific passwords.

children.name: example.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "=== 18: Master macOS Systems Drill ==="
echo "1. XNU Mach + BSD Architecture"
echo "2. SIP Protection & TCC Security"
echo "3. APFS Copy-on-Write Clones"
echo "4. Universal 2 Mach-O binaries"
echo "🚀 You have completed the comprehensive macOS Mastery Track!"
